articles.title: The Millennium Falcon Is Great but These 5 Star Wars Ships Are the Coolest of Them All

articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Star Wars looked very different from the other sci-fi we had seen before 1977. In the '50s and '60s, the Golden Age of Sci-Fi, we pictured clean, orderly, high-tech futures, but Star Wars went a different direction. While there was more than its share of sleek, modern tech, most of it was used, "lived-in", beaten up like '70s America. The best example of this is the Millennium Falcon . Known as the "fastest hunk of junk in the galaxy", Han Solo and Chewbacca's YT-1300 light freighter was heavily modified, with souped-up engines, military-grade shields, armor, and weapons, and a specialized computer system to run it all (I say, computer, but in canon and Legends, it's actually a bunch of droid brains rigged together).

It was the first personal ship we saw in Star Wars , but it wouldn't be the last. Over the years, in both canon and Star Wars Legends , we've seen all kinds of awesome ships, owned by the best pilots and modified to high heaven. As great as the Falcon is, there are some ships that are way cooler, including these five designs from canon and Legends.

People love to compare Star Wars canon to Legends , but it's honestly kind of a boring comparison. Both have their high points (as I'll try to illustrate at various places) and one of the highest points for both was the first Thrawn Trilogy. These three books – Heir to the Empire, Dark Force Rising, and The Last Command – introduced numerous amazing characters, including the smuggler Talon Kardde. Kardde built up a massive illegal empire under everyone's noses and had a small fleet of smuggler vessels, including the Wild Kardde . A modified Corellian Engineering Corporation Action VI Bulk Freighter, it was a very unique vessel and the flagship of his fleet, alongside the Etherway and the Starry Ice .

To begin with, it was a massive bulk freighter, meaning that Kardde and crew could hide just about anything in its cavernous holds. It had a very powerful power plant, allowing Kardde to give the ship military-grade weapons, shields, and sensors. It had thick armor and was armed with three turbolasers, each of them hidden in the hull until needed. It could shoot it out with the big ships, could run from the fastest chase craft, and looked so assuming it could go anywhere. It's a favorite of many Legends fans.

Disney's tenure in control of Lucasfilm gets a bad rep, but it has introduced some amazing Star Wars characters over the years, including the incomparable Din Djarin, the Mandalorian. Din has had quite a journey over the course of the series, one that started out with the Razor's Crest . I'm an old school Legends fan and I loved the Razor's Crest immediately. It had just the right feel and look for a bounty hunter ship. It looked like a standard freighter, lightly armed, and nondescript, exactly the kind of ship you'd see anywhere.

Manufactured by the Corellian Engineering Corporation and Belsmuth Consolidations Ltd., it was a ST-70 M-111 Razor Crest series. Djarin souped up the engines and cannons, making it faster than it looked and letting it pack a stronger punch, and it had a cool look to it. It did end up getting destroyed by the Empire on Tython, but he'd get another one. It helped give The Mandalorian that Legends feel that really did it for me in the show's beginning.

The '90s were a better time than they seemed to be a Star Wars fan. Sure, there was no movies or TV shows, but there were books, comics, toys, role-playing games, and video games. In 1996, we got the multimedia project Star Wars: Shadow of the Empire , which consisted of a novel, comics, RPG supplements, toys, and a N64 video game. It introduced several cool new characters including Dash Rander, a Corellian smuggler. He was basically a Han wannabe – the story took place between Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Jedi , so he was frozen in carbonite and the story needed a scoundrel – down to his souped Corellian freighter, the Outrider .

It was a YT-2400, a newer generation than the Falcon . It was almost as fast in hyperspace, but faster at sublight, and had powerful shields and weapons, including two double laser turrets and concussion missile launchers. It was basically the Falcon if it was better kept up and has more than its share of fans. It also appeared in the Special Edition of Episode IV in 1997, so it's technically canon.

Mara Jade is the great lost Legends character . Fans have wanted her brought into canon even if she can't marry Luke Skywalker for years now. The former Emperor's Hand was a powerful Force using assassin before she met Luke. He brought her to the light and she eventually trained as a Jedi, marrying him at the end of the war against the Empire. The two of them led the New Jedi Order through the Yuuzhan Vong War and the Joiner War, but she'd end killed in the Second Galactic Civil War. In the last few years of her life, she flew the Jade Shadow , a SoroSuub Horizon -class star yacht.

It was heavily modified, with powerful shields and engines. It was armed with retractable laser cannons, a retractable blaster cannon, concussion missile launchers, and a tractor beam projector. Jade had the ship specially designed for her, with a special cockpit that would allow her to control every station herself from the helm. Jade was one of the best pilots in the galaxy, so the Jade Shadow handled like a starfighter despite being 55 meters long. She was fast and powerful, an amazing ship for an amazing woman.

Star Wars: Skeleton Crew was an underrated gem and it's the type of show that shows that we shouldn't just give up on canon, even if we get lackluster stuff like The Acolyte or The Mandalorian and Grogu . The show followed a group of children who found a hidden pirate chip and fly into the stars, on the course of adventure. It was basically Goonies meets Star Wars and it's fantastic. That ship is the Onyx Cinder . It was a vessel that was commissioned years ago by the Galactic Republic, one of its treasury ships meant to transport credit ingots from the Republic mint on At Attin.

It was stolen by pirates at some point before the fall of the Republic, used by captains like Tak Rennod and Jod Na Nawood. It was everything you could want from pirate ship – it was fast, durable, and it had a secret, as its hull was just an armored sleeve for the real Onyx Cinder . I loved this ship from the second I saw it. It just looks awesome. It's the kind of ship that anyone would want to command – fast, durable,and powerful – with a cool secret that hides an even better design.

What Star Wars ships do you like more the Millennium Falcon ? Or do you think it can't be topped? Sound off in the comment section below.

articles.summary: The latest Nintendo GameCube game on Nintendo Switch Online has now arrived on the subscription platform. articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The latest Nintendo GameCube game on Nintendo Switch Online has now arrived on the subscription platform. Throughout 2026, Nintendo has slowly been bringing classic GameCube titles to Switch Online for those who happen to own a Switch 2. While this GameCube library is still pretty slim, it contains some of the all-time best games that appeared on the platform such as The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker , Luigi's Mansion , Super Mario Sunshine , and Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance . Now, Nintendo has added its 12th game to this growing lineup of GameCube titles on NSO, and it's one that subscribers weren't anticipating.

Starting today, Wave Race: Blue Storm is available to play via Nintendo Switch Online's GameCube catalog. Released in November 2001, Wave Race: Blue Storm is primarily synonymous with the GameCube as it was a launch game for the platform. As the sequel to the N64 classic Wave Race 64 , Blue Storm features roughly the same gameplay as its predecessor, with players racing jetskis against one another across a variety of different maps.

Although it might not be as popular as Wave Race 64 , Blue Storm was still plenty popular amongst GameCube owners. As a result, it's addition to Nintendo Switch Online is very much a welcome one to those subscribed at the Expansion Pack tier of the service.

"Take to the water in this watercraft-racing game, released for the Nintendo GameCube system in 2001," says the game's description. Compete in contests of speed and technique—either racing against your rivals or going up against your own records. As you race across the waves, you can see the skies changes from calm and sunny to surging storms. Weather conditions can affect visibility, water levels, and the height of the waves over the course of a race, so you'll need to be prepared for whatever comes!"

While it's a very nice surprise to see Wave Race: Blue Storm now available through Nintendo Switch Online, it does continue to raise one big question. Specifically, Nintendo previously announced well over a year ago that Pokemon Colosseum would be coming to NSO in the future. Instead, Nintendo's latest two additions to this GameCube library, Star Fox Adventures and now Wave Race: Blue Storm , were ones that it previously didn't reveal would be coming to the subscription platform. For these games to have arrived prior to Pokemon Colosseum is a bit odd and only raises further questions about when this Pokemon spin-off might become available.

The good news is that Nintendo hasn't announced that Pokemon Colosseum is no longer planned to join Nintendo Switch Online. As a result, it might simply be waiting for the right opportunity to pull the trigger. With Pokemon Day set to take place in February 2027, perhaps we'll see the GameCube classic added to Switch Online around this time.

Until then, what do you think about Wave Race: Blue Storm joining NSO today? Are you going to look to play this returning classic for yourself? Be sure to let me know down in the comments.

A month after the former Fear Factor host inked a more than $200 million multi-year contract extension with Spotify for the Joe Rogan Experience, a just released report says Rogan is the most trusted figure in media by almost half the men surveyed.

Adding to the texture of that result is a deeper dive that one-time MAGA kingmaker Rogan is considered the Walter Cronkite of our age by 41% of Democrats in the Beyond The Manosphere study from Precision Strategies and Tunnl Data.

While Rogan tops the trust list, he is closely followed by Stephen A. Smith (38%) among the 3,001 men Precision and Tunnl surveyed last month. Breaking down the pre-midterms data further, potential POTUS candidate and Donald Trump dining companion Smith is trailed as a info source by The Charlie Kirk Show , fellow ESPNer Pat McAfee, Ben Shapiro and ex-Fox News top dog Tucker Carlson .

The dominance of conservative voices should be an alert to Democrats who are chest pounding over their big midterm elections wins, and how fragile that new coalition could be. At the same time, the pronounced shifts against buddy Trump that Rogan has articulated of late with slams against the stalemated Iran war that no one wants to be in" and the immigration abductions from “militarized police in the streets wearing masks."

Just over two years after endorsing Trump and six months after calling fights at the UFC Freedom 250 matches at the White House, Rogan a week ago seemed to returning to his old stomping ground of being a Bernie Sanders fan. "They didn’t just lose the podcast bros," the JRE host said on his November 13 podcast of the midterm rout of MAGA and the GOP. "They lost most of the country." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In testosterone territory, where video games are the primary community for the podcast bros, note the total Top 5 absence of traditional media like network and cable news anchors. They don't exist. "Men and women share the same core of YouTube , Facebook, Instagram, and TikTok," Sam Fitz, Precision's SVP, Data & Analytics, tells Deadline. "YouTube is the center of gravity for both: 89% of men use it in a typical week, compared to 84% of women."

A national survey of 6,046 adults (3,001 men and 3,045 women), the 2026 report is also very telling on a number of levels of the Bowling Alone generation legacy and the so-called crisis among American males that has been assumed as an undercurrent to the populism and political upheaval of the last decade.

Or, put another way, Joe Rogan is helping to heal Daddy issues.

The latest look by Precision, which was founded in 2015 by ex-Democratic operative and White House aide Stephanie Cutter, at the much analyzed Manosphere spotlights that "nearly two-thirds of men (63%) say there is no man in their life they turn to for advice." That Daddy or male authority figure deficit gets worse as income levels go down. The study from the integrated strategy and marketing agency states that "70% of men in households earning under $50,000 have no male mentor, as do 68% of rural men."

"This tells me that when asked directly, men seem to differentiate between who informs them and who guides them," Precision's Fitz notes of the male mentor gap the study reveals. "They have plenty of the former, and are sorely lacking when it comes to the latter. But that said, even if they don't identify this themselves, it's fair to assume that men without 'mentors' will fill the gap with Joe Rogan and other popular online content creators that talk through the issues men are dealing with."

Touching on topics of faith, race, money, marriage, family, culture and GLP-1 weight-loss drugs, the Manosphere study isn't just about the fellas.

In fact, looking at the data from the women surveyed may be one of the most telling aspects of the whole thing.

While men seem to be more of media monolith with Team Rogan, women have far more and a greater diversity of trusted sources. Granted no single female trusted media source gets even half the pull of Rogan, the breakdown reflects the shift of the last decade ideologically and otherwise.

To that, Not Gonna Lie podcast host Kylie Kelce is number #1 among women with the allegiance of 22% of those surveyed. Worth noting, self-declared left leaning Democrat Kelce has constantly given Rogan a run for his money and even beaten the UFC announcer in term of listeners and downloads since the September 2024 debut of Not Gonna Lie.

After Kelce, who also appears in various other media with her spouse and ex-NFLer Jason Kelce, Megyn Kelly comes next for trusted source status among women. The rest of the Top 5 is filled out by conservative commentator Candace Owens, Call Her Daddy founder Alex Cooper, and former NCAA All-American and anti-trans activist Riley Gaines.

With the right-ish preference of the men and women surveyed, a tendency to limit certain Constituational rights is also shined up in the Manosphere survey — one MAGA, DSA, Republicans, Democrats and Independents should pay serious attention to. In a landscape where faith in the government is lacking, "31% of men and 26% of women say the government should be able to limit press access for outlets it considers unfair or untruthful," Precision's SVP Fitz says of the study. "This jumps to about 50% for Republicans, men and women alike." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

If all those lawsuits, credential revoking and "fake news" bluster is any indication, that last stat may be the Trump takeaway.

articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producer Explains Why No Last Airbender or Korra Writers Return
articles.summary: Nickelodeon Avatar: Seven Havens introduces a new room of writers to the franchise, and the showrunner behind it all has explained why they decided against bringing back any of the writers from Avatar: The Last Airbender or The Legend of Korra. The new era of the franchise has been a big success with Paramount+ thus far […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Avatar: Seven Havens introduces a new room of writers to the franchise, and the showrunner behind it all has explained why they decided against bringing back any of the writers from Avatar: The Last Airbender or The Legend of Korra. The new era of the franchise has been a big success with Paramount+ thus far as the first season of the series has done well with both critics and fans . And much of that success has been thanks to the fact it feels so fresh.

Avatar: Seven Havens not only introduces an entirely different kind of art style and animation than seen with its predecessors , but the writers behind the series are all new as well. When asked about the choice to not bring back any of the writers from the older shows in a recent Reddit AMA , executive producer Sehaj Sethi explained that they "wanted to create a room with new voices who I felt could really flesh out these new characters." It was a deliberate choice to go this route.

"While I deeply respect and admire all the writers on the previous two series, I wanted to create a room with new voices who I felt could really flesh out these new characters," Sehaji explained about the approach to Avatar: Seven Havens ' writing. "We had racial and gender parity between all the writers, and I think that really helped bring a lot of depth and complexity to the storytelling." But even if the episodes don't have previous show writers , the franchise has been overseen by the original creators.

When putting Avatar: Seven Havens together, Sehaj revealed that original franchise creators Michael DiMartino and Bryan Konietzko already had the idea of setting it within a post-apocalyptic world in mind . "Mike and Bryan approached me with this concept already in mind," the producer began. "I think they had been noodling with setting the next series far into the future for a while. There were definitely challenges to creating seven brand new, unique city-states and cultures, but it was also freeing to be able to bring a lot of new ideas and concepts to the franchise."

Avatar: Seven Havens has also been put together in a much more concrete way than with The Legend of Korra too. DiMartino previously explained that unlike its predecessor where it was initially planned out to have just a single season for its story, Avatar: Seven Havens has been developed with a clear end goal in mind from the start . While the number of seasons didn't really settle until Paramount+ gave the all clear, the team had an idea of where they were going and how to get there.

Avatar: Seven Havens has confirmed that it will eventually come to an end with four seasons under its belt. Season 2 of the animated series is currently scheduled to make its debut with Paramount+ next May, and Season 3 will then follow later in 2027. The fourth season has yet to confirm a release date or window as of this time, but at least fans can rest easy knowing that this team has a firm plan in mind. But how are you feeling about Avatar: Seven Havens ' writing so far? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes’ Ex-Assistant Speaks Out on ‘You Can See Everything’ and Amanda Seyfried’s ‘Valid’ Performance: Holmes ‘Softened a Lot in the Film’
articles.summary: For Aria Marinelli, "You Can See Everything" hit a little close to home. Marinelli, who worked as Elizabeth Holmes’ assistant in 2009, during the early stages of Theranos, spoke about watching her former boss in the documentary in an interview with Warner Bailey on "AvA Live." "My initial reaction was I did not want to […]
articles.content:
For Aria Marinelli, " You Can See Everything " hit a little close to home.

Marinelli, who worked as Elizabeth Holmes ' assistant in 2009, during the early stages of Theranos, spoke about watching her former boss in the documentary in an interview with Warner Bailey on "AvA Live."

"My initial reaction was I did not want to see it," Marinelli said of the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim film. But then, eventually, "I acquiesced and went out of sheer morbid curiosity, and I came out of there just feeling really contemplative. I mean, she's a real human that I interacted with, and to see her up there going to jail with children was really emotionally charged for me, as someone who does have a kid as well." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Natalie Portman to Present Sundance's Inaugural Women Filmmakers Award as Part of Fest's New Dior Partnership Sanaa Lathan and Terence Blanchard Join Sundance Winner ‘Jazz Infernal’ as Executive Producers (EXCLUSIVE)

When "You Can See Everything" surprise premiered at Telluride and became one of the buzziest films of the year, Marinelli, who has rarely spoken about her time at Theranos 17 years ago, realized, "I have a voice in this too. [Holmes] doesn't get to be the one to just come back on the scene and control the narrative."

Marinelli called the film a "crazy, wonderful, thoughtful, strategic piece," and praised Fielder's ability to portray Holmes as she truly is. "I do think he's done it justice."

Compared to her time running the fraudulent blood-testing startup, "She seems like she's softened a lot in the film," Marinelli said of Holmes. "But she still seems like she really wants to win."

Amanda Seyfried plays a big part in "You Can See Everything," reprising her role as Holmes in reenactments with Fielder after the Theranos founder went to prison. One of the tension points in the three-hour A24 film is Seyfried's portrayal of Holmes in the hit Hulu miniseries "The Dropout." Billy Evans, Holmes' romantic partner, clashes with Seyfried in the movie as he accuses her (and everyone else who worked on the series) of peddling lies about Holmes for the sake of entertainment. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Marinelli, who knew Holmes intimately in 2009, said watching "The Dropout" was "remarkable" because "I can vouch for a lot of that." (As an example: "I remember she listened to rap music really loud.")

Asked if she thought Seyfried's depiction of Holmes was "fair," Marinelli said, "Yeah, I do, because a lot of the things I saw were measured and valid. Obviously they're dramatized, because it needs to keep people's interest. But there was nothing I saw that seemed out of sorts with what I knew to be true."

Holmes is currently serving a 10-year prison sentence and is expected to be released in 2030. In the film, she and Evans tell Fielder they are working on a new biotech startup, continuing the progress of Theranos.

As to whether Holmes deserves a second chance, Marinelli said, "I think people are complex, and we always deserve second chances. It might not be the best idea to go into the same field where you've already burned all the bridges, very publicly. It's a complex question, and not for me to answer, because she needs to decide the direction her life takes after something like that. I can't imagine what it must feel like to reset, especially if she truly believes she was following her dream. But yeah, I think we all deserve a second chance."

articles.title: Taylor Swift’s Wedding Was The A-List Event Of The Year And Also Incredibly Awkward For Conan
articles.summary: The wedding of the century was not all magical for Conan O'Brien.
articles.content:
Even though it’s November, people still can’t stop talking about the wedding of the year, Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce . The power couple officially tied the knot during the Fourth of July weekend at Madison Square Garden , and there was plenty of talk both before and after the nuptials. It seemed like everyone who was anyone attended . However, the event has made it incredibly awkward for Conan O’Brien.

Of course, Swift and Kelce went all out for the surprisingly intimate wedding , and that includes inviting a range of celebrities who you never thought would even be in the same room. Or even if you did think about it, you’d never imagine you’d see it... let alone hear about it. For O’Brien, no matter how many celebrities he’s interviewed over the years or is friends with, he still couldn’t wrap his mind around who all was at the wedding. And he wanted to place himself inside that group:

Seeing a grouping like that would be pretty incredible, and it sounds like O’Brien and his wife were both in awe. I can’t say I blame them being in that environment. Unfortunately, despite being at the wedding like them and having a pretty tight relationship with likely a lot of people there, O’Brien couldn’t exactly push his way into the trio. While he ultimately didn’t move in on them, he could only imagine what would've happened, especially since he hadn’t yet met one of them. He went on:

That definitely would be super awkward. Imagine going over to them, having never met Phoebe Waller-Bridge and just getting straight-up rejected. I wouldn’t be surprised if he had thought about it almost the entire time he was at the wedding. Of course, there’s no telling what would have actually happened, and Colman even said that Waller-Bridge is “wonderful.” Although being in that setting and surrounded by those kinds of people, I can see where O’Brien’s hesitation would come in.

articles.title: Diablo 5 Has Already Revealed Its First Three Classes, & They're Perfect For Diablo 3 Fans
articles.summary: Courtesy of Blizzard Entertainment While Diablo 5 isn't coming out for the next few years, Blizzard has revealed the core classes for the next entry in the dark fantasy action RPG series. These archetypes are both brand-new and familiar, with two of them actually being past classes from other Diablo games that veteran fans might recognize easily. Despite not […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google While Diablo 5 isn't coming out for the next few years, Blizzard has revealed the core classes for the next entry in the dark fantasy action RPG series. These archetypes are both brand-new and familiar, with two of them actually being past classes from other Diablo games that veteran fans might recognize easily. Despite not knowing anything about how Diablo 5 's core gameplay and character builds will differ from past Diablo titles, these classes should give players a great first glance at the game's starting direction.

There are some classes that have been in almost every Diablo game, such as the Sorcerer, Barbarian, Necromancer, and a couple others. However, Diablo 5 seems interested in establishing an identity fairly unique to the series, with the story being set in a world where evil has already won and characters are isolated sources of hope in a ravaged wasteland. As such, the new classes do a better job at reflecting this new reality, with several gameplay system changes in Diablo 5 teasing a much different experience than players are used to with Diablo 4 's long life cycle.

The surprising announcement of Diablo 5 at BlizzCon 2026 has led to a steady trickle of information about the game, from a planned 2029 release window to the first three classes. These classes were revealed in shared concept illustrations, but only represent the start of Diablo 5 , with Blizzard promising "more classes than ever before" in the final version of the game. The classes announced are the ones listed below, along with some details regarding their planned play styles within the game:

The Plague Knight is one of the most interesting concepts here, taking a darker or "evil" archetype concept seen in other Diablo classes like the Necromancer or Witch Doctor from past games. Those classes could return too, but it's fascinating to see the Plague Knight take the Diablo series in a new direction that players didn't really expect. The abilities of the Plague Knight are somewhat of a mystery beyond its teased explanation by Blizzard, though players can expect a tank-like character path that utilizes heavy armor more than other classes. With loot and gear of Diablo 5 said to be inspired by Diablo 2 , there will be plenty of opportunities to explore unique Plague Knight builds.

On the other hand, the other two classes coming to Diablo 5 were both present in Diablo 3 , with the Demon Hunter being a totally new archetype for that game back during its 2012 release date. The Demon Hunter is somewhat of a replacement of Diablo 's Rogue class, albeit with new shadow powers and a stylish use of twin crossbows to give the archetype more flair than cloaks and daggers. In fact, the Demon Hunter was likely one of the most beloved classes in Diablo 3 , as its nimble ranged attacks provided a unique play style compared to the melee focused Crusader or Barbarian.

The Demon Hunter also stood out in Diablo 3 for being the only reliable ranged attacking class that didn't rely on magic, like the Wizard or Witch Doctor. This mobile assassin could place traps to take down enemies, or use shadow magic to teleport across the screen, easily making it the most elusive class in Diablo 3 . If anything about the Demon Hunter's tool kit is re-created for Diablo 5 , it could easily become a fan-favorite once again, especially in Diablo 5 's seemingly oppressive world where danger lurks around every corner.

The Monk is another popular Diablo 3 class too, arguably providing the most interesting melee play style in that game compared to the heavy weapons and armor of the Barbarian or Crusader. Monks are the only class in the series to use Fist weapons, but they are something of a jack-of-all-trades when it comes to character builds. This class can be molded into a pure tank, a DPS machine, or a supportive figure for multiplayer parties. This is due to the Monk's resilient abilities, which include helpful auras for allies, devastating stunning melee attacks, or defensive skills depending on how players build their character. This versatility is great alongside the other Diablo 5 classes, especially if the archetype is fleshed out more.

The return of the Monk and Demon Hunter shows that Diablo 5 is paying homage to Diablo 3 way more than other games in the series, continuing a trend from other entries. Diablo 4 brought back Diablo 2 classes in full force, while establishing unique ones of its own, such as the Spiritborn later introduced through expansions. That being said, Diablo 5 might be trying less to replicate the best parts of Diablo 2 , and instead try to correct some pitfalls of Diablo 3 through new design choices in the character classes players select. The Plague Knight is the best example of this, as it could be a completely overhauled Witch Doctor from that game.

In many ways, the Plague Knight could be everything the Witch Doctor was not, existing as a stronger variant of a class that uses disruptive, disease-focused abilities to swarm enemies. The Witch Doctor in Diablo 3 was often a less liked class in the game, being described as a knock-off Necromancer for using horde allies, AoE effects, and debuff afflictions to define its play style. While the Plague Knight is set to be more defensive and tank focused than the Witch Doctor ever could be, it may also adopt some of these design choices, taking the Witch Doctor's abilities into its own alongside new skills.

It wouldn't be surprising to see the Plague Knight use the same horde tactics as the Witch Doctor, or have large AoE effects on certain abilities that mimic that class' strategy from Diablo 3 . However, the variety of the class will undoubtedly be increased more through Plague Knight gear or aesthetics, making it less similar to the Necromancer. With the Demon Hunter and Monk not needing to change as much, Diablo 5 has the best chance to give Diablo 3 fans what they want, while also correcting some of that game's failings when it comes to character class design.

What class do you want to play the most in Diablo 5 ? Let us know in the comments below!

articles.content:
Tidal , a formerly artist-backed music streamer that is now majority-owned by Twitter co-founder Jack Dorsey's Block, is taking an aggressive stand against AI .

Citing a massive surge of artificially created music, the company on Tuesday announced a complete ban taking effect on December 9. As of that date, the company said in a post on X that any wholly AI track detected on the platform will be "rejected and removed."

In the past 90 days, the company says, 43% of all tracks on its platform have been detected as wholly AI-generated. Tidal labeled them (a step many other companies have also been taking) and removed them from its royalty pool. articles.title: A Weird Little Sci-fi Show With Puppets Changed TV and Movies Forever 38 Years Ago
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Comedy Central The '80s were a wild time in the United States. I was born in 1980, into a world that was rapidly changing. The hippie kids of the '60s and early '70s were adults and voted Ronald Reagan into office with a resouning landslide electoral victory two months after I was born, throwing away love and […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google The '80s were a wild time in the United States. I was born in 1980, into a world that was rapidly changing. The hippie kids of the '60s and early '70s were adults and voted Ronald Reagan into office with a resouning landslide electoral victory two months after I was born, throwing away love and LSD for profit and cocaine, the year ending with the death of John Lennon, almost as if the iconoclastic spirit of the '60s decided that they wanted off this ride before it got worse. These two events might not seem related, but they changed pop culture forever. The hippies sold out and that's why we are where we are right now. However, not all of them did. The '80s were also a time of wild art and experimentation, as a new generation of kids rebelled and created punk, post-punk, new wave, and goth. A whole generation of artists took the spirit of the '60s and put it in play in a way that the generation that experienced didn't. A perfect example of this is Mystery Science Theater 3000 .

Myster Science Theater 3000 is one of those venerable pieces of pop culture that had a massive effect on everything, but most people who weren't there don't even know it existed. The show was the brainchild of Joel Hodgson. He had grown up during the B-movie explosion of the '50s and '60s, and had a love for those terrible old movies. He pitched the show to St. Paul, Minnesota's KTMA-TV (now known as WUCW) in 1988, where it would air and gain a cult following, leading to it becoming the flagship of the early Comedy Channel before it merged with the other comedy channel, with Mystery Science Theater 3000 airing on Comedy Central until it ended in 1996. It completely changed the pop culture landscape in ways you'd never imagine.

Nowadays, you can go on YouTube and find a hundred thousand different movie review channels. There's the ones you expect – just a person talking about a film – and then there's the ones where the hosts have built up a whole universe outside of their reviews. They review the movies in character and each review tells it own story in their continuing narrative (can anyone email me a Pizza Roll?). Some of them have recurring characters, guest stars, and the like. You can find a channel like this for basically any piece of pop culture you like, across just about any genre. It's just the way it is now.

However, before 1988, there wasn't really anything like that on TV. Sure, there was Siskel & Ebert At the Movies , which was fantastic, and critics would appear on a variety of talk and news show, but it was all played straight. Mystery Science Theater 3000 was something completely new when it started; Hodgson created his own story to be a part of the show, to keep people tuned in to these terrible old movies. Like many people in the '80s, Hodgson had spent years watching bad B-movies and making fun of them with his friends. This sort of thing has always been a rite of passage, and Hodgson brought that to audiences in Minnesota and then across the country.

The premise of Mystery Science Theater 3000 is simple – Hodgson played Joel Robinson, a person who kidnapped by mad scientists, referred to as "the Mads", and imprisoned on the Satellite of Love , named after the classic Lou Reed song (here's a reference not all of you will get – "shine a light of love" – but you all know who said it). In order to stay sane, Robinson ended up building sentient robots, named Tom Servo, Crow T. Robot, the station operations manager GPC (formerly named after the common slur used against the Romani people), and Cambot. The group of them would watch the worst movies you can ever imagine, making fun of them the whole way.

My stepdad was a guy who loved bad black and white sci-fi B-movies, and we would often rent them and watch them, making fun of them the entire time. Hodgson did the same with his friends on the shows, except he did it in such a way that matched the spirit of those old B-movies. The low budget sci-fi movies of the '50s and '60s were some of the weirdest, cheesiest things imaginable, and MST3K, the most common abbreviation of the show's name, tapped into that spirit.

I think one of the things that we miss about those old movies, and why MST3K was such a success, was that they were often labors of love. Look at someone like legendary B-movie director Ed Wood. He loved the stories he told. Roger Corman is known as one of the most efficient directors in the history of Hollywood, churning out low budget movies like nobody else, but does anyone doubt that he loved what he was doing? These old movies were labors of love, and MST3K was to tap into that, both by lovingly (and not so lovingly) mocking these movies while also using their tropes and ideas and also by being one itself.

The show would run for one season in St. Paul, moving to the Comedy Channel in 1989, which eventually morph into Comedy Central. Starting in 1991, MST3K was the flagship for the channel. People tuned into the show, allowing the network to get more successful and bring us classics like The Daily Show and South Park . The only reason we have Comedy Central at all is because MST3K was there, getting viewers and selling merch. It was one of the best cult '80s TV shows of its day. Hodgson would eventually leave the show due to creative differences with co-producer Jim Mallon, as well as his own discomfort for being on camera, ending an era of the show.

He would be replaced by Mike Nelson, played by actor Michael J. Nelson, and then Nelson would be replaced by Jonah Heston, played by Jonah Ray. The show ended in 1996, just in time for DVDs to make it way easier to sell entire seasons of TV (I once bought an entire season of a show on VHS in the '90s; it was expensive and took up several feet of space). All new audiences were introduced to the show and its format. Many of these people would end up using the Internet to do their own spin on the MST3K formula, allowing YouTube to become an entertainment juggernaut, all on the back of a show that the nerdiest people you knew in the '90s loved.

Mystery Science Theater 3000 's legend has grown and grown over the years. For a very particular kind of nerd in the '90s, MST3K was mana from the heavens. It gave them a sense of community and inspiration, leading a whole generation to create their own little worlds in order to do a fun movie review show. The spirit of MST3K inspired people like the Angry Video Game Nerd, the Nostalgia Critic and the rest of Channel Awesome, and the Red Letter Media guys, for better and for worse. It's a massive part of the DNA of YouTube, which itself has changed the face of pop culture in a variety of ways.

Sometimes, I like to think about the people who changed the world in strange ways. Most of these people never expected to become such important part of pop culture; most of them probably still don't even realize how integral they are to the world. Joel Hodgson creating Mystery Science Theater 3000 in 1988 was the first domino that would lead to our pop cultural world. He legitimately played a huge role in building our current entertainment paradigm and he did it by making fun of bad movies with his puppets. Fans have brought the show back numerous times, with it returning in 2017 and eventually becoming RiffTrax. Mystery Science Theater 3000 will always be one of the most important shows ever made, even if most people never knew about it.

What do you think of Mystery Science Theater 3000 ? Were you a fan? How do you feel about its place in pop culture? Sound off in the comment section below.

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google One major creator has returned to the pages of Shueisha's Weekly Shonen Jump magazine only a year after their previous series came to an end, and has kicked things off with a special crossover to help celebrate. Shonen Jump has entered its final transitional period for the year as a number of titles have kicked off their own serializations as fans say goodbye to some of the longer running hits . But with this go around, some of these new titles are from experienced creators.

Hitsuji Gondaira wrapped up Mission: Yozakura Family 's run with Shonen Jump last year , and has already made his return to the magazine with the start of a new series. Making its debut over the weekend, Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol offers a much different kind of story than seen with the chaotic spy adventures of Gondaira's previous work. As a special way to celebrate the new debut, Gondaira has released a special crossover with Hizuki and Taiyo joining the Ginza Patrol. Check it out below.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol made its full debut with Shonen Jump this past weekend , and the first chapter of the new series offers an entirely different kind of story than fans had seen with Mission: Yozakura Family. While that series offered an extended cast as Taiyo joined a huge family of spies, this new series doesn't go that route. Instead fans are introduced to Osamu Hizuki, a samurai who's come out of the war with the intent of living a life enjoying the new era and its technologies.

Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol already seems a lot more focused when it comes to its core cast as there's really only Hizuki and his new partner Rin. She's the first girl to join the patrol, and is only doing so to eventually solve the murder of her mother. Hizuki was one of the most deadly samurai in the war, but hopes to leave that life behind eventually and enjoy his new life. We'll see how this all develops as the series hopefully gets the chance to have as long of a run as Mission: Yozakura Family was able to before it ended .

Shonen Jump is an incredibly fickle magazine as this year alone has already seen 14 different titles come to their ends. Only six of those releases were titles that were able to come to their natural conclusions , and all of the others had been cancelled shortly into their respective runs. It's hard to tell at this point if Gondaira's newest work has any real chance of success, but it's likely to avoid cancellation at least for a while since it's a returning creator already familiar with how Shonen Jump operates.

That's not always the best thing for Shonen Jump , however, as even some returning creators have had their new works cancelled after short runs. It doesn't matter how successful their prior work is either as with notable cases like Masashi Kishimoto's Samurai 8 getting cancelled after a few months despite how big of a runaway hit Naruto was before. It's all a toss up.

How are you feeling about Hizuki of the Ginza Patrol so far? Do you think it has a chance at success with Shonen Jump ? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: "Alarming" Diversity Backtrack Happening In Film and TV Industry In Canada, Report Finds
articles.summary: Despite homegrown hits like 'Heated Rivalry' and 'North of North,' the Writers Guild of Canada warns “key barriers” to future work stand in the way of new diverse members joining its ranks.
articles.content:
As the Canadian film and TV industry remains committed to diversity, equity and inclusion, resisting pressures to backtrack in a post-Trump DEI rollback era, aspiring diverse screenwriters now find themselves struggling to advance in a shrinking business.

So says the Writers Guild of Canada in its latest Equity, Diversity and Inclusion report released on Tuesday.

While the guild pointed to more diverse screenwriters joining its Canadian ranks, WGC executive director Victoria Shen revealed in the report “alarming numbers that affect not only diverse writers, but all Canadian screenwriters. This is the second year in a row in which we saw a decline in the number of episodes across every production format covered by the report. While we have seen decreases in Canadian production in the past, these numbers demonstrate an industry in decline.”

The EDI report accounted for diverse writers in the WGC ranks by measuring the number of black, indigenous, LGBTQ2S, people of color and people with disabilities. And the percentage of diverse members in the WGC membership rose to 51 percent in 2025, up from 42 percent in 2024 and 33 percent in 2019.

Despite that membership growth, the 2026 EDI report pointed to the number of writers earning over CAN$200,000 (US$140,000) being highest among white, cisgender, heterosexual and non-disabled writer, while half of black writers and those with disabilities earned less than CAN$20,000 (US$14,000) in 2025, the last year measured.

Amid mounting industry disruption, domestic broadcasters continue to lose market share to foreign streamers, who in turn face no local content spending obligations to offset lower investment in the Canadian ecosystem. And that’s impacting diverse Canadian writers who rely on local content investment to get in the door and build careers.

“One of the key barriers to their advancement is the depressed state of the industry and the lack of opportunities for anyone, which is compounded and made more acute by their diverse identities,” Shen insisted. The Canadian TV industry has faced a continuing contraction as audiences and advertising dollars shift to U.S. streamers and other digital platforms.

And that has implications for Canadian sovereignty versus the country’s southern neighbor amid U.S. President Donald Trump’s ongoing tariff war and taunts about Canada becoming the 51st state.

“Investment in Canadian culture is more important now than ever. The loss of jobs for Canadian screenwriters is the bellwether that spells the loss of our screens to foreign creators. But this time of profound change is also an opportunity to reimagine what is possible. We can do more than defend Canadian culture: we should realize its economic potential, bolster its cultural reach and export it. Investing in Canadian screenwriting and domestic production is how we start to reverse the decline and reform the industry,” Shen argued.

The latest EDI report from the WGC surveyed 141 series live-action and animation series produced in 2024 and 2025, in addition to the 448 series covered from 2019 to 2023.

The guild found a steep decline in production numbers from 2018 to 2025, including 29 percent fewer one hour drama episodes at the end of that period, and 28 percent half-hour adult series episodes.

The WGC also pointed to even steeper cuts in the number of kids live action and animation episodes.

articles.title: Fans of Nathan Fillion's Wrongly Canceled Sci-Fi Western Series Can Grab His Screen-Matched Pistol for $15,000
articles.summary: Courtesy of 20th Century Studios When it comes to TV shows that were canceled before their time, there are a handful that still sting no matter how much time passes. Among them is a sci-fi series that debuted in 2002 to almost perfect reviews from audiences but didn't even make it to the end of its first season before being […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google When it comes to TV shows that were canceled before their time, there are a handful that still sting no matter how much time passes. Among them is a sci-fi series that debuted in 2002 to almost perfect reviews from audiences but didn't even make it to the end of its first season before being canceled, much to the annoyance of those who had very quickly come to love it. Starring Nathan Fillion, Firefly is one of the biggest missed chances in TV history, and even though there has been talk of a possible revival , a live-action return has not happened so far. Yet the love for the series among fans has never waned, and now thanks to Prop Store fans have the chance to own the Liberty Hammer pistol used by Fillion in his role as Captain Malcolm Reynolds, but it won't come cheap.

The sidearm that is up for auction is not just a regular prop gun either. This one has been screen-matched to Firefly sequel movie Serenity , after being used in the series first and later modified with a removable magazine. It is also one of only two weapons made for the show that could actually be fired. The gun was adapted from a real Taurus Model 85 revolver, with brass-colored frame, a spring-loaded slider, and brown wooden grips. Although the piece was real at the time of filming, the gun has since been fully deactivated and comes with a certificate of proof. Of course, this means that the price tag will reflect the scarcity of the item, and after already hitting its starting bid of $15,000 the estimate suggests that price will rise to up to $60,000. If the right interested parties are in attendance as the auction closes on December 4, then the final price could end even higher.

There are not many TV shows that are canceled after one season then go on to be among some of the most-loved and remembered. Firefly only managed to air 11 episodes before being pulled from schedules by Fox, with three additional episodes never airing. However, when the series was released on DVD, the show gained a cult following that refused to let it die. This momentum was enough for the characters from the series to get a second chance with a big screen adventure in Serenity . The movie released in 2005 to rave reviews just like Firefly , even if its box office did not match the praise. The film ended up making $40 million, but considering its $39 million budget it did not spark any studio interest in reviving the series or developing a sequel no matter how much the fandom wanted it.

Many members of the Firefly cast have gone on to bigger things, including Morena Baccarin, Alan Tudyk , and, of course, Fillion, who most recently became the DCU's new Green Lantern in 2025's Superman . However, even 23 years after their last outing, the cast of Firefly have not given up on coming back together for a revival and it is now happening in an animated series . Yet the idea of the show being brought back to life in a live-action format has also not gone away. While there are certainly no guarantees of that coming to fruition, there could not be a better time for Firefly to make a return with streamers constantly looking for their next hit. Could it be possible for a new series of Firefly to actually make it to screens and be the success that was denied of its first run? Stranger things have happened.

Would you love to see Firefly return? Let us know in the comments.

Since launching back in 2024, Marvel Rivals has continued to be one of the most popular multiplayer games across consoles and PC. While the game features playable versions of Marvel icons like Spider-Man, Hulk, Captain America, and Iron Man, it has also introduced some much lesser-known Marvel characters that players have become more familiar with. Now, one of these breakout stars of Marvel Rivals has become so beloved in their own right that LEGO has opted to create a new toy based on their in-game look.

Revealed today on LEGO's official websit e, the toy manufacturer showed off a first glimpse of a new model for the character Jeff the Land Shark. Upon the arrival of Marvel Rivals , Jeff was one of the first playable characters on the game's roster. Although he was relatively unknown at the time, Jeff has since become arguably the face of Marvel Rivals , and remains one of its most beloved Marvel heroes nearly two years after its launch.

As for this LEGO version of Jeff the Land Shark, it's set to launch right at the start of 2027 on January 1st. The set, which is number #67023, includes 495 pieces in total and will come in at a price of $49.99. Generally speaking, this is a pretty solid price-per-piece value, which should lead to Jeff the Land Shark becoming one of the more popular and cost-effective LEGO sets to begin the new year.

You can get a look at this Jeff the Land Shark LEGO model for yourself right here:

Moving forward, there's a chance that LEGO could look to release more products that are tied to characters from Marvel Rivals . However, if this were to happen, LEGO would likely have to find a way to differentiate these sets from the countless other Marvel products it has released over the years. Characters like Spider-Man, Iron Man, and Hulk are no stranger to having been remade in LEGO fashion, which means that the brand would likely have to figure out what would set them apart if they were to get recreated in a Marvel Rivals -style. It's hard to know just now what this might look like, but it's still promising to think about as we look ahead to the future.

articles.content:
Thank goodness for Aunt Gladys. If it weren't for last year's fright-wigged "Weapons" villainess — a bracing figure of pure, malicious evil amid cinema's recent run of goody-two-shoes witches, sparkling up the likes of "Wicked" and "Practical Magic 2" — you'd begin to worry that screen sorcery has altogether lost its edge. Not that there's anything wrong with humanizing witches per se , but surely we can all agree that the bad ones have more fun. The new Disney animated feature " Hexed " splits the difference. Its suburban teenage heroine Billie is about as wholesome a witch as witchery has ever seen, but at least she enjoys her powers, instead of moping about them: After the "Wicked" films spent nearly five hours telling us it's not easy being green, the chief takeaway of the bright, chipper "Hexed" is that witchin' is bitchin'. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-variety-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Amazon Debuts $30 Streaming Bundle That Includes Starz, BritBox, AMC+, MGM+ and PBS Masterpiece In One Place Celebrity Streaming and Commerce Platform TalkShopLive Expands to TikTok Ahead of Black Friday

There's not a whole lot more to it than that, however, even as Fawn Veerasunthorn and Jason Hand 's film attempts to squeeze a mother-daughter bonding tale in amidst all the magical hijinks. "Hexed" is ostensibly the first original animated film from the Disney stable since 2023's swiftly forgotten "Wish," but it certainly doesn't feel that way: Quilting together story elements from any number of previous, occult-tinged coming-of-age tales, it's about as familiar as, well, a witch's right-hand cat: Even its lurid violet-and-jade color palette looks secondhand so soon after "Wicked's" ubiquitous green-and-pink branding.

From its cookie-cutter characterization to its throwback design elements to a soundtrack embellished with familiar pop songs, the film is altogether too risk-averse to threaten classic status. That its narrative, about an ordinary American girl stumbling into an enchanted realm and discovering her hidden supernatural genes, bears some resemblance to that of the recent stop-motion stunner "Wildwood" — down to the flocks of malevolent ravens flapping about the place — can be only be coincidental, but "Hexed" isn't especially flattered by the comparison. It is, however, an emphatically more kid-friendly enterprise, and with "The Cat in the Hat" fizzling at the box office, the Disney pic should make hay with families over the Thanksgiving weekend. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[320,480],[300,250],[300,251],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366],[300,450]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

A tone of chatty irreverence is struck by the opening prologue, which lays out a fairytale backstory in jagged, collage-style animation: a witch-ruled queendom, a power struggle, the loss or misplacement of magical powers that our blasé narrator describes as "a real bummer." She doesn't sound that invested, so neither are we. But as we begin the story proper in modern-day Salem, our interest is sparked in adorable, saucer-eyed newborn Billie — seemingly a typical baby girl, doted on by her single mom Alice (Rashida Jones), until one night in her crib, she demonstrates literal, lightning-like magic in her fingertips. Sadly the intriguing prospect of a telekinetic infant is quashed when, following a near escape from an otherworldly portal accidentally opened up by the tot, Alice neutralizes Billie's powers with an unprepossessing bracelet, and leaves Salem for Blahville, Ohio.

Sixteen-odd years later, Billie (now peppily voiced by Hailee Steinfeld ) is a strong-willed high-schooler wholly unaware of her powers, and chafing against her mom's constant, chiding attempts to control her. When the latest of Billie's rogue escapades gets her expelled from school, Alice decides again to leave town — at which point Billie, who has somehow never removed her safety bracelet until now, finally does so, and is immediately whooshed away into the magical realm of Hexe, and is immediately shown the strength of her witchy capabilities.

Those include flying — rare even among her newfound kind, and an immediate threat to Queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), the silver-coiffed sorceress who rules over Hexe with chic cruelty. Soon exasperatedly following her through the portal is Alice, who it turns out knows Hexe — and Celeste — all too well: No surprise that Billie's powers are hereditary, and that it falls to mother and daughter to save the embattled queendom, with some crotchety assistance from Beef (Walton Goggins), a three-eyed, Southern-drawled feline familiar who looks a little like Disney's Cheshire Cat as misremembered by ChatGPT. Goggins' ripe vernacular delivery is the most pleasingly unexpected element here: Everything else runs pretty much entirely according to studio-blueprinted plan, down to the breakneck, back-and-forth chase of a finale in which the real duel for dominance plays out on the soundtrack: Demi Lovato's "Confident" battles composer Kris Bowers' busy orchestrations to a cacophonous draw.

“Have you ever been persecuted, drowned or burned at the stake?” Conditions for entry to the city of Hexe are pretty rigorous and surprisingly dark in this engaging Disney animation. After playing things safe with 2023’s almost immediately forgettable, formulaic Wish , the studio has somehow turned the tanker round with a surprisingly edgy Y.A. fantasy that sometimes seems in danger of going too far in the opposite direction. Mention of warlocks in the stylish prologue is a little misleading; Hexed is a film about witches all the way, a hectic but mostly very entertaining fantasy that seems curiously beholden to Wicked , in ways that threaten to seriously undermine everything that’s good about it. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Casting Hailee Steinfeld Confirms She's In 'Avengers: Doomsday' News How Jodie Foster Took Her First Disney Voice Role In 'Hexed' And Lent Her Smile To Her Character - Contenders L.A.

Girl power is the central theme, introducing Billie Doe ( Hailee Steinfeld ) as an Ohio infant with special powers, whose mother Alice ( Rashida Jones ) watches over her with a cautious eye after almost losing her to a couple of crows that once appeared through a portal to another world. Fast-forward a few years, and Billie is now going through her difficult teenage years, borrowing her mother’s car without permission (or a licence) to set the school mascot — significantly, an owl — free into the wild. The headmaster is on the warpath, but, while hiding in the bathroom, Billie manifests a strange ability to move things with her mind. Billie’s supernatural talents are somehow connected to a bracelet she has been forced to wear since childhood, and after she takes it off for a second time, the portal returns and sucks her into a parallel dimension. After being inducted by a talking book and a pen (Stephen Fry and Tracey Ullman respectively), Billie becomes a citizen of Hexe, a sanctuary city for practitioners of the occult. Hexe, though, is not quite the land of the free that it first appears to be; under the reign of Queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), it is very much a two-tier society, divided into those who indulge its narcissistic ruler and those who don’t. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

For reasons that seem fairly obvious already, Alice follows her daughter to Hexe and tries to send her home in an enchanted cauldron while she distracts the local police chief. Instead, however, Billie follows the cryptic label on a magic potion that leads her to Beef Roger Crummchuk ( Walton Goggins ), a three-eyed cat and one-time familiar to Queen Celeste’s daughter. After an extended sequence in which Billie begs for his help — lots of scenes gone on far too long — Beef Roger decides to help Billie look for Alice, who is now locked up behind barred doors and windows in a tower at the royal palace.

Comparisons with Wicked were always going to be inevitable, but the extent to which Hexed leans into them goes way beyond homage, notably in Queen Celeste’s fleet of flying bird-women with creepy fluorescent eyes. Hexe itself even looks like Emerald City, and when Billie first embarks on her adventure, she tells Beef Roger that “We’re gonna yellow-brick-road it”, the only time The Wizard of Oz is consciously mentioned. And once again, the climax involves the unmasking of an impostor, as Queen Celeste manipulates the talents of others to perform a centuries-old moon spell and gain ultimate power.

There’s still a lot to like, however, especially in its use of witchcraft as a metaphor; much play is made of Billie’s teenage-emo awkwardness, with her purple hair, spindly legs and clunky goth boots (“You think there’s something wrong with me,” she wails to her long-suffering mother). Surprisingly, there is no father in the picture, and the story boils down to an interesting three-way dynamic between Alice, her daughter and the Queen, one that doesn’t quite take the direction you might be expecting. A great and very eclectic voice cast helps in this regard, with Goggins a surprisingly calming presence whenever things get hectic (and they do).

But while Foster’s frosty Queen Celeste offers a refreshing return to the unreconstructed Disney villainesses of old, the rest of Hexed can’t help but seem retrofitted to get us there. There are welcome shades of Zootopia in its world-building — notably a town of familiars, and a rowdy pirate bar — but the story takes some strange turns, especially when, as Queen Celeste’s plan is about to unfold, we go back, albeit briefly, to Ohio. Its message — the usual be-yourself, do-your-thing — is harmless enough, mind. It’s just disappointing that a film so high on intention, ignition and inwitchification should fall so short in the inspiration department. There’s still enough potential for a sequel, mind.
