articles.title: 'Focker-in-Law' Filmmaker John Hamburg Talks Ariana Grande's Comedic Timing and the Actor Who Made Ben Stiller Laugh Hardest on Set
articles.summary: Hamburg, whose credits include 'Me Time,' 'Why Him?,' 'I Love You, Man' and 'Along Came Polly,' reveals his writing technique and shares what it was like to be challenged by Grande: "She can dial it up or down and give me so many different levels."
articles.content:
It's been 26 years since Universal Pictures introduced Greg Focker to his girlfriend Pam's parents, Jack and Dina Byrnes, and audiences responded in kind — to the tune of $330 million worldwide. A franchise was born that year, and it has since produced 2004's Meet the Fockers , 2010's Little Fockers and the latest, Focker-in-Law , due in theaters Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday. John Hamburg, who has been with the franchise since the beginning as a writer (and later as a producer), jumped into the director's chair on Focker-in-Law to direct a cast that includes returnees Ben Stiller , Robert De Niro , Teri Polo, Blythe Danner and Owen Wilson with new additions Ariana Grande , Skyler Gisondo , Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco. The Hollywood Reporter caught up recently with Hamburg on Zoom to talk about landing a global pop superstar for the cast, his writing process and who makes Stiller laugh the hardest on set. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Music Ariana Grande, Peacock Team on 'Eternal Sunshine Tour' Doc, Concert Film Movies 'Focker In-Law' Review: Ariana Grande Outshines Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller in an Otherwise Dire Fourth Installment

In 2020, you spoke with one of my colleagues who asked about the possibility of another movie. At the time you said, "I'll refrain from answering, but I love everyone involved, we’re all still in touch, and that’s all I’m going to say." An obvious follow-up: What happened?

I’m still asking myself that question. The core group has been making these movies for 26 years, and we check in from time to time. We only wanted to revisit these characters we love so much if we had a story we needed to tell. It wasn’t worth doing for the sake of it. Then we had a nugget: Ben Stiller is roughly the same age Robert De Niro was when we made the first movie, which is insane, but it gave us a way in. The first movie had an organic setup many people can relate to [bringing a significant other home to meet your parents], and it lead perfectly into the second. You met one set of parents, now it was time to meet the second set of in-laws. I don't think we had that clean of an idea for the third movie, which is maybe it was not quite as strong as the first two. For this movie, we looked inward and came to the conclusion that we wanted to get back to the simplicity of the original Meet the Parents. We had themes and ideas that we liked but it wasn't until we created the Olivia Jones character that everything came together. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Were you coming up with ideas and then taking it to the team, or brainstorming during meetings?

We did a little development when I was only producing. Once I came on as a writer, I explored different directions and we met over Zoom with the team — Ben, De Niro, Jane Rosenthal, Jay Roach and John Lesher — to talk things through. Then I went off into to a dark room to figure it out. I had the idea that Greg Focker’s nemesis could be his son’s girlfriend: a powerful, complex, formidable woman who is the opposite of Greg in every way he was 30 years ago. That felt compelling. I pitched to Jay Roach early on and asked what he thought.

In our conversations, Jay suggested different jobs she could have. I think that’s how we landed on the idea of her being a hostage negotiator. That clicked for me because suddenly I saw the central conflict: She thinks Greg is holding his son emotionally hostage by being such an overly involved parent. I got excited and pitched the team again. They liked it. I wrote a treatment of about 20 pages, telling the story and coming up with the pieces. After that, I had to fill everything in: Where is De Niro in his life? Who is Samantha, Beanie Feldstein’s character? Who is Henry, his son? But it all started with that idea.

I’m curious about your “dark room” strategy and how it’s changed over the years. When you need to lock yourself away and be productive, what does that look like for you? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

I write in 25-minute increments. There’s a productivity technique called the Pomodoro Technique . You shut everything off for 25 minutes and focus completely, then take a five-minute break and do the next one. If I get six of those in a day, I can be pretty productive. When I was rewriting the script during pre-production, I did 13 or 14 Pomodoros a day. There’s also a lot of hand-wringing and walking around my neighborhood. There are tears and moments when I think, "I can’t figure this story out. I don’t know what to do." It was challenging. Once I got the Olivia Jones character, the rest flowed quite smoothly.

Did you write with anyone in mind? At what point did Ariana Grande come into the mix?

If people are attached, I write with them in mind. I knew I was writing for Ben Stiller, Robert De Niro, Owen Wilson, Blythe Danner, Teri Polo and the others. But when I’m writing a script or early drafts, I usually want to make the characters real to me first. It’s almost like a police sketch of different people. I knew the energy and vibe, but wasn’t sure who would play the roles. Once I finished and put on my director's hat, I started thinking about who it could be. We landed on Ariana and said, "That's it. She has to be the one." I just hoped she would say yes because she was the only person I could think of, for a variety of reasons.

There are many wonderful actresses, but Ariana is such a force. The fact that she hasn’t been in a million movies makes her almost mysterious, which appealed to me. I’d watch her on Saturday Night Live and marvel at her incredible comic timing and think, "She's hilarious. She gets it." I also liked that she could be surprising. She has a twinkle in her eye and isn’t physically imposing, but the idea of someone who looks like Ariana Grande completely destroying Ben Stiller felt like a conflict we could really exploit. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

She pulls it off amazingly well. What was it like to direct her?

She's unbelievably smart, had a great handle on the character and pushed me to do more and try different things. As a writer, that’s what you want: someone who will challenge you and push you in the best ways, always in service of the story and character. She certainly did that. It's hard to believe she’s been in so few movies because she’s so skilled and has such a big toolbox. She can dial it up or down and give me so many different levels. That's great as a director: In the editing room, you can craft the performance and dial it up or down.

She announced that she was stepping away from public life. How did you respond to that news?

I love Ariana and have so much affection for her as a human being. When I heard the news, I also heard she was going to support the movie. We talk, and I know she loves it. I want whatever's best for her. At the end of the day, this is a business about human beings, and I adore her. I got to see her in concert in London this summer. It was moving to watch how her audience responds to her. She’s so powerful and gives so much. I thought, "My God, I can’t imagine what it’s like to give so much of yourself night after night." The key thing is that she said yes to the movie, and I know she’ll support it in whatever way feels right to her.

I got the chance to interview Skyler Gisondo for his recent Bonobos campaign and he told me that while he was shooting your movie with Ben Stiller, he didn't realize until he was on set how much he had borrowed from Ben during their first collaboration on The Night at the Museum franchise. What was it like to direct Ben and Skyler together? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid4' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

It was amazing. Skyler is one of those actors I’ve wanted to work with. You see someone like him in his movies, whether it's Booksmart or Licorice Pizza , and think, "I've got to work with that guy." I really liked the idea of Skyler as Henry Focker. I didn’t think it was a problem that he’d played Ben’s son before becuase it had been so long. I thought they’d have a shorthand, and they fell into it so quickly and were perfect. They both work hard and want to try different things. They push themselves to find nuance in the characters. I definitely saw Ben’s influence on Skyler. I could tell Skyler wasn’t just on set; he’d been taking it all in like a sponge. When you have someone like Ben Stiller — unbelievably funny and smart, and one of the hardest workers — that’s a great person to learn from. A lot of the movie's heart comes from the father-son relationship. There’s a really sweet moment between them at the end, and their real-life affection and long connection helped.

You've worked with Ben Stiller for years. When you're on set, what's the rhythm like?

One of the great things about our long relationship is that it's a real collaboration — a back-and-forth, a push-pull. He can pitch me things, and I can pitch him things. It's always about the character, the story and making it better. One thing I learned from Ben very early on, probably when we were working on Zoolander a thousand years ago, is never to settle. Keep pushing and trying things because they can always evolve and get a little better. He still has that ethos today. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid5' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Directing Bob was truly one of the great joys of this experience. I’d directed Ben before and collaborated with him on many projects. I’d known Bob for years, primarily as a writer on the Meet the Parents movies. I’d helped him on a couple of other movies, uncredited, and was a writer-producer on the third one. But to direct him was a joy. He's Robert De Niro; his talent and filmography are second to none. What inspired me was that, at 82, he still had so much passion and enthusiasm. He'd call me late at night to pitch ideas, or share ideas constantly by email or text: "What about this for this scene?" How incredible is that? He has great instincts for Jack Burns and for how to humanize him.

You've also worked closely with Owen Wilson, who makes a fun return in this movie. Can you talk a bit about writing those scenes and working Owen?

I love Owen so much. I had the best time directing him in Stick . There’s no one like him: He has such a unique rhythm in the way he speaks and moves through life. It's so much fun to write a character who can say the most absurd things with a smile and no self-awareness. I can't have every character lack self-awareness, but Owen can parachute into the movie for a stretch and play that kind of character. In this movie, I thought about where he’d be in life. He has twins and thinks he's parenting them one-on-one, with no help, while there’s an army of nannies and caretakers everywhere. In his mind, he doesn’t believe he has any help; he’s raising the kids by himself. It’s so much fun to write. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid6' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

One of the other great joys is that no one makes Ben laugh like Owen Wilson. They’re so different, so close, and have made so many great movies together, but they live life as total opposites. Owen cracks Ben up; he just has his number. It’s so much fun to watch them enjoy each other’s company between takes. When the camera’s rolling, there’s a tension that’s fun to film and explore.

What was the most challenging nut to crack?

It started with figuring out who Greg Focker’s adversary would be, which I've touched on. But the most challenging scene was probably the bike race. In my early drafts, it was on a tennis court, and that didn’t work for a variety of reasons. I also knew Ben was into the Tour de France and cycled himself, so I thought he might like it. A director friend who read it said, "Why'd you do a bike scene? They’re so hard to shoot." It was a nightmare, but we had the right team in place, and it went smoothly. Set pieces can’t be there just for their own sake; they have to be about character and the tension between the characters. I had to figure out the setting and the sport. The Meet the Parents movies have a tradition of a sport going wrong — pool volleyball in the first movie, football in the second — so I knew I’d have a sports scene. I just didn’t land on it until later in the process.

In an interview, Barbra Streisand revealed that she was still upset over her salary for the Fockers . Were you close to getting her for this movie, or were there conversations? blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid7' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

Barbra and Dustin are such a part of the Fockerverse , and I’m grateful every day that they were in those two movies. With this movie, I really wanted to return to the simplicity of the original Meet the Parents. Sequels can get bigger, with more and more characters, so I set this movie in the Burns family home, where the original took place, and tried to keep it contained. I love Dustin and Barbra. We did talk about it, of course, because they’re part of our Focker family. But with so many new characters in this generation, it ultimately felt right to focus on the characters we ended up with.

People keep talking about the challenging landscape for feature film comedies in theaters. How hard is it to be a comedy writer and filmmaker in the business right now? Do you feel the pressure?

When these movies are made well, there’s nothing better than sitting with 400 people who are all laughing and cringing. That’s why I got into this business: I loved going to the movies and laughing my butt off. I mourned the fact that comedies disappeared from studio film slates and theaters. They moved to streaming, which is great, but it’s not quite the same for a movie like this. That also sets up all the different ways people will see the movie later. I’m hopeful. I just wrote and directed a movie that’s being released in theaters, so of course I have some skin in the game. But I do think people are realizing that we need to be together. Watching things alone at home or on our phones is great for some things, but it isn’t everything. I’m optimistic this genre can come back. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid8' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

As for pressure, my comedy-director friends are constantly asking, "How did the movie test? Is it good? Is this movie going to work?" I tell them it tested great. I don’t know how it will do, but I feel good about it. I do feel some pressure because I love this genre. It’s given me everything in my career, and I’m hopeful we can get back to a place where these movies are seen in theaters again.

When was the last time you saw something and reached out to say, "God, that was funny,” or “I loved that”?

Literally the other day. I saw an ad Ben Stiller did for his soda brand, Stiller Soda. He goes to Canter’s Deli, gets it wrong, and is dressed like he’s in the cast of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats . It was hysterical. I texted him a crying-laughing emoji. It was pretty damn funny. And my God, the Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim movie — the first half had me thinking, "Wow, there are big laughs in this. Huge laughs." It’s so awkward, but it was really funny. I don’t know those guys, so I didn’t text them, but I’m a fan.

articles.title: ‘Hexed’ Review: Hailee Steinfeld and Rashida Jones Lead a Disney Fantasy More Enchanting in Its Spectacle Than Its Storytelling
articles.summary: Jodie Foster and Walton Goggins also lend their voices to the animated adventure about a teenager who discovers she's a witch and gets transported to a magical realm.
articles.content:
There’s a sequence midway through Hexed , Disney’s animated fantasy adventure, when mother-daughter heroines Alice ( Rashida Jones ) and Billie ( Hailee Steinfeld ) are forced to retreat to a remote lakeside cabin. Coming just after a brutal face-off with the wicked queen Celeste ( Jodie Foster ), the scene is heavy with emotion; whether they’re able to pull off a miraculous recovery here will determine the fate of not only their mission, but their very lives.

Amid all that fear and hope and desperate love, however, I found myself overcome by an incongruous surge of envy. As I looked around the hideaway, with its giant windows and twinkly fairy lights, its big fluffy couch perfect for napping and its rustic shelves crammed with plants and candles and otherworldly knickknacks, I couldn't help thinking: I would kill to rent this place on Airbnb . blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories Movies Hailee Steinfeld on Recording Music for New Movie 'Hexed' and Becoming a Mother in the Process Movies Jodie Foster Describes 'F1' as a Movie "Made by AI" at Aspen Ideas Fest: "I Don't Say This Disparagingly" Hexed The Bottom Line You've heard this story, but you haven't seen this world. Release date: Wednesday, Nov. 25 Cast: Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones, Walton Goggins, Jodie Foster, Dan Stevens, Henry Winkler Directors: Fawn Veerasunthorn, Jason Hand Screenwriters: Jared Bush, Dana Ledoux Miller Rated PG, 1 hour 43 minutes

It wasn’t the first time watching the film that I’d wished I could walk right into the screen, though it was surely the only time I could imagine the rental listing so clearly. More than as a fairy tale, an inspirational fable or a complex exploration of the bonds between mothers and daughters, Hexed shines brightest as a travelogue through an enchanting world only accessible through the portal of a screen. If that’s not enough to make for a new cinematic classic, it’s more than enough to make for a pleasurably transportive trip to the theater.

The actual premise, as scripted by Jared Bush and Dana Ledoux Miller (the recent live-action Moana ) and directed by Fawn Veerasunthorn ( Wish ) and Jason Hand ( Moana 2 ), is a hodgepodge of sturdy but shopworn clichés. Like teens everywhere since time immemorial, Billie (Steinfeld) has never quite felt like she fits in. Unlike most teens, Billie turns out to have a very good reason for feeling this way. A dust-up at her suburban Ohio high school reveals Billie to be not an ordinary girl but a witch, her powers suppressed at infancy by her overprotective mother, Alice. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid","mid-article2","mid-articleX"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

In short order, Billie finds herself transported to Hexe, a magical realm awaiting the fulfillment of a prophecy by a chosen one who will finally bring true freedom and safety to all of its people. Blah blah blah, and so on and so forth; Hexed doesn’t seem especially interested in the specifics of this situation, so you needn’t concern yourself with them either. The more important thing is that this plot functions very capably as an excuse to zip around the land of Hexe, which is where the real fun lies.

As experienced through Billie and then Alice — you didn’t expect this helicopter mom not to have a Find My Kid app installed, did you? — Hexe is a riotous feast of deep colors, rich textures and undulating shapes. It is both the film’s blessing and its curse that a standard phone or laptop, of the sort you may have used to view the trailer, cannot do it justice. What looks merely messy on an eight-inch screen looks wonderfully immersive on a 20-foot one, the frame crowded with so much fine detail it seems impossible to take it all in at once.

Courtesy of production designer Lorelay Bové, the characters dance through Disney-land cute towns, trudge through Avatar -alien swamps, curl up in goblincore dens packed with funny little cat tchotchkes. In my very favorite sequence, they don animal disguises to infiltrate a no-humans-allowed dive where a cockroach and a spider are engaging in a WWE-style match, down to a teeny-tiny folding chair. The imaginative world-building extends to an amusingly idiosyncratic supporting cast. Walton Goggins steals every one of his scenes as Beef Roger Crummchuk, a green three-eyed cat who’d rather be drinking martinis alone in his magically expanded swamp RV. Lazy and cantankerous in equal measure, he’s both the film’s most reliable comic highlight and its unexpected heart — the cynic who goes from insisting that “it’s safer to stay home licking your armpit” since “most battles aren't worth fighting” anyway to finding a renewed sense of hope in Billie’s determined heroism.

Really, the whole ensemble is an embarrassment of riches, with even one-scene characters played by the very recognizable likes of Jimmy O. Yang or Ron Funches or Stephen Fry. It’s surely an expensive flex from Disney, but it’s one that pays off. Hexe feels as vivid as it does because Hexed misses no opportunity to stuff in a bit more humor or personality or strangeness around the margins. A tense conversation with the queen might be punctuated by a tiny teacup exclaiming, “Baby, you’re cooked ” in the voice of Yvette Nicole Brown, or an impromptu spell-casting practice session interrupted by the complaints of a microwave voiced by Wayne Knight.

In comparison to all the bewitching delights and exotic thrills of Hexe, Billie and Alice almost cannot help but pale in comparison. As plucky Disney heroines, they're plenty likable, just not especially unique. Jones gets some lovely bittersweet notes to play as Alice’s deep emotional wounds come to the fore — often thanks to Foster’s Celeste, whose true viciousness cuts all the deeper for how persuasively she can play kind and benevolent when it suits her. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-thr-article-mid-articleX-uid3' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["btf","mid-articleX","mid"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4]]) .setLazyLoadMultiplier(2) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

articles.title: Four-Day Rom-Com Film Festival to Launch in Santa Barbara
articles.summary: The inaugural event is set for April 22–25, 2027.
articles.content:
Romantic comedies are feeling the love.

The genre is getting its own cinematic celebration with the inaugural Rom-Com Film Festival, launching in Santa Barbara April 22- 25, 2027. The event will bring together filmmakers and audiences for four days of toasting the classics and discovering new stories, after being founded by Carissa Buffel, Kevin Matusow and Kate Bacon of women-owned production company The Traveling Picture Show Company.

“ Rom-coms make people smile. It’s really as simple as that. We wanted to create a festival that celebrates this beloved genre and brings people together in a lighthearted and happy way," Bacon said in a statement. Screenings will take place across multiple venues in downtown Santa Barbara, including the McHurley Film Center and the Santa Barbara Museum of Art, with an additional outdoor screening experience in the works. Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google A new dark fantasy Isekai anime is coming to Crunchyroll this January, and has now locked down its release date with a new trailer and poster showing it all off. With the ongoing slate of Fall 2026 anime releases now rounding out their respective final phases, it's time to look ahead to all of the new releases coming our way next year. And 2027 looks like it's going to be kicking things off on the right foot for Isekai anime fans with one series in particular.

The anime adaptation for Yu Shimizu and Makoto Aogiri's Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! was originally scheduled for a release in Fall 2025 before being hit by a major production delay behind the scenes. But it's finally now set a release date of January 7th next year as part of the upcoming Winter 2027 slate. To commemorate the release of the new series, you can check out the new trailer and poster for the upcoming Isekai below.

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! is currently scheduled to release in Japan on January 7th, and will be streaming exclusively with Crunchyroll when it finally makes its debut. There have been quite a few shake ups behind the scenes following its two year delay too with Naoya Fukushi now directing the series for Studio Durandal with Mamoru Yokota and Yui Kato providing the character designs, Yui Horiguchi serving as CG director, Hiroshi Hosokawa providing the scripts, and Asami Tachibana composing the music.

It's also been confirmed that Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! will feature the opening theme titled "Sai" as performed by LIL LEAGUE, and an ending theme titled "Zanka" as performed by ZAQ. Both of which have been previewed in this newly released trailer. The voice cast for the series includes Kazuki Ura as Yukito Kirihara, Kana Yuki as Charlotte R. Brownia, Yui Ishikawa as Lumilia Sherwood, Kaori Maeda as Liverna Dark, Hika Tsukishiro as Sana Kirihara, Fukushi Ochiai as Rocinante, Ayasa Ito as Managarmr, Yoko Hikasa as Nephilia Curse, Anri Katsu as the narrator, and Yuichiro Umehara as Sharaza.

Otherworldly Munchkin: Let's Speedrun the Dungeon with Only 1 HP! takes a dark path much like some of the Isekai anime releases that have gotten a lot of attention from fans in the last few years. Yukito and his sister are suddenly transported to another world, but he's got a major disadvantage in exploring it. When he's brought to this new world he's given a mysterious character sheet and given all sorts of random properties by a mysterious woman.

Discovering he only has a single hit point, Yukito needs to navigate this mysterious new world and find his sister all while dealing with some strange new threats. There's some of kind of underlying threat underneath it all, and that always leads to some great results with Isekai anime of this kind. With so many other new Isekai coming our way next year , what are you hoping to see in action in 2027? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments.

articles.title: Chris Evans Just Confirmed a Big Avengers: Doomsday Theory, And Marvel Fans Shouldn't Be Surprised
articles.summary: Marvel Studios Robert Downey Jr. is wearing that Doom mask for all of Avengers: Doomsday, and that's according to MCU favorite Chris Evans. Since Marvel Studios confirmed that the Oscar-winning Downey would return to the fold but take on the part of Doctor Doom rather than Tony Stark, fans have speculated about the real reason behind it. […]
articles.content:
Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Robert Downey Jr. is wearing that Doom mask for all of Avengers: Doomsday , and that's according to MCU favorite Chris Evans . Since Marvel Studios confirmed that the Oscar-winning Downey would return to the fold but take on the part of Doctor Doom rather than Tony Stark, fans have speculated about the real reason behind it . Could Doom be some kind of variant of Iron Man, or vice versa? In any event, every Marvel fan is already bracing for the moment that Doom's mask comes off on screen and the MCU heroes see that familiar face, if they do at all.

Speaking with Empire , though, Chris Evans says that Robert Downey Jr. keeps the mask on for the entire movie. “He's wearing a mask the whole time," Evans said. "That's not an easy challenge, to try and get your message across and be emotionally available to connect with. It just reinforces what I've always felt: Downey can do anything.” The Captain America star's confirmation about Doomsday seems to squash any fan theory about Downey's face being seen in the film as a big reveal…or does it?

It's worth reiterating that Evans said his co-star is "wearing a mask the entire time," and not "you never see Robert Downey Jr.'s face." Evans could be truthful here about how often Doom is wearing his signature mask; it would be in keeping with decades of comic book canon (though Anthony Mackie already spilled the beans that "it wasn't" him on set sometimes ), but that doesn't mean that there won't be a moment where Doom is isolated and takes it off for a moment.

That said, it's also easy to see why a performer like Robert Downey Jr. would be able to reach the emotional depths required of Victor Von Doom and the tragic backstory that has pushed him to his limits , despite wearing a mask; it's all about how he uses his eyes across the film. Though we've only seen so much footage of Doom in the trailers for the film, the close-ups of his eyes reveal that there's a nuanced performance happening under there.

If it ends up being true that Robert Downey Jr. is wearing his Doom mask for the entire film, it could be because Marvel is saving the big unmasking moment for Avengers: Secret Wars . Fans are already bracing for RDJ's villain to win at the end of the day and set up the next big crossover movie, which could very well be where Tony Stark's former allies see the villain who destroyed the multiverse bear a striking resemblance to the hero that saved their own world. It will be a devastating reveal at any point, but it simply remains to be seen when Marvel decides to deploy it.

What do you think? Is Evans telling the truth, and does Robert Downey Jr. wears the Doom mask the entire movie? Or is he simply preserving the Marvel spoiler secrets and we'll see him without the mask at some point? Sound off with your thoughts in the comments below and let us know.

articles.title: Josh Allen on 'The Buffalo Miracle,' and What a Miracle It Would Be to Bring Buffalo a Super Bowl
articles.summary: The superstar quarterback's production company Out of Pocket is off to a hot start — much like the 9-1 Bills.
articles.content:
Buffalo is the coldest place with the warmest neighbors.

That dichotomy of sorts is on full display in HBO 's The Buffalo Miracle , an Oscar-qualifying documentary short executive produced by Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen , among others. The Buffalo Miracle tells the story of the Buffalo, New York residents who came together during the deadly Christmas blizzard of 2022. Their refuge? McDonald's store #34815.

Though Allen is the big name here, The Buffalo Miracle centers on a different, shorter local hero: McDonald's manager Kristin Kosha bucked corporate protocol, unlocking the fast-food restaurant's doors to more than 50 stranded, freezing residents as the historic storm grew increasingly dangerous. (Also north of 50? The inches of snow dumped by the Dec. 23-27 blizzard.) Lives were saved and bonds were formed. And oh yeah, there was a Bills game to watch and pass the time — they crushed the Chicago Bears in Chicago, 35-13, clinching the AFC East. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-article-mid-article-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid-articleX","mid","mid-article"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[300,250],[2,2],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[320,480],[620,366],[300,450],[4,4],[300,251]]) .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories TV Archie Renaux on 'War's Resident -- and Misunderstood -- Bad Boy TV 'The Gilded Age' Scores Season 5 Renewal at HBO

"I love it! It’s not every day you get to see yourself drawn as a cartoon," Kosha said. "Honestly, it made me laugh, but it also made me feel a little emotional. Out of Pocket was announced just before the NFL Regular Season. You're CEO, you're going to executive produce all of the output: How much time, if any, will you be able to dedicate to Out of Pocket during the football season?

I mean, it's not going to be every single week. But given certain… whether we have a Thursday night game, if we can get on a phone call and talk with my team, who's been doing a fantastic job, and just run down what's going on. Watching shorts and seeing if we want to attach our name with them.

But this one kind of coincidentally came up right when we launched. We got introduced to Ben [Proudfoot] from a mutual friend, and it just worked out perfectly. What are your immediate plans for Out of Pocket once your season ends?

We've got some cool projects coming up. We've got a scripted show that I can't talk a lot about, but just got sold, and we're working on that right now. That's going to be awesome. Do you have any ambition to act?

I don't think so. I think staying behind the camera is the best option for me. I'll let my wife get in front.

You're extremely creative on the football field. Do you believe the creative football mind informs the creative artistic mind and vice-versa?

Yeah, I pride myself on the creativity that I have on the football field, and I think in order— the football field, in my opinion, is the truest version of who you are as a person, right? That is everything stripped off. That is you going out there and you are letting your emotions show. They're like 35 minutes north. I have not been to that McDonald's, but I get to meet Kristin and (assistant manager) Jeff Spengler tonight, so that'll be really fun.

I'm not gonna lie, I'm a Big Mac guy, and give me 10 nuggets and a large fry. And you've gotta have the Oreo McFlurry.

The Bills have never won a Super Bowl. When they famously lost four straight in the '90s, you hadn't yet been born. Do you think you're able to understand how much a Super Bowl win would mean to Buffalo?

I think so. I've come to grips with [the fact that] I think it's going to mean more to the city than it will to me personally. articles.title: Fans Were Mad After A Wedding Guest Ignored Miley Cyrus’ Dress Code. Now, Her Sister Spoke Out
articles.summary: Some think she came in like a wrecking ball. Her sister came to her defense.
articles.content:
At Miley Cyrus and Maxx Morando’s wedding , all the guests were wearing black. Well, all except one, who stood out because they wore yellow instead. Now, as this moment goes viral, the sister of the guest who seemingly ignored the dress code has come to her defense to explain how this slip-up happened and how the “Wrecking Ball” singer reacted to it.

While Cyrus’ big day made headlines because of how gorgeous it was and how she paid tribute to Dolly Parton during it, this celebrity fashion faux pas has also gotten a lot of attention. The guest who wore yellow is Belgica Vargas, the wife of the music producer Shawn Everett, and in photos from the ceremony, she can be seen in a yellow outfit among a sea of people wearing black. The photo caused many people on Reddit to comment things like:

Meanwhile, many others on Reddit gave her the benefit of the doubt, saying she probably missed the memo on the dress code. Those more sympathetic Reddit commenters wrote things like:

Then, there was a whole camp of folks who were upset about there being a dress code in the first place. So, all around, this yellow outfit is causing quite the stir online. However, Vargas’ sister has popped into the comments to clarify how this seemingly happened.

It turns out that comment about the woman in yellow just never getting the memo about the dress code was a great guess. As this fashion slip up went viral, Vargas sister, Grecia commented on a video of someone zooming in on her sibling’s dress. Explaining that her sister was not aware of the dress code, she wrote:

Listen, it’s easy to miss details sometimes. articles.title: Tidal Bans Wholly AI-Generated Music: "Serious Problem That Has Only Increased in Scale"
articles.summary: The service said Tuesday that more than 60 percent of new tracks uploaded to its service on Nov. 6 were fully AI-generated songs.
articles.content:
Tidal is outlawing wholly AI-generated music from its platform, the streaming service announced on Tuesday, saying that AI music "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans."

"To ensure Tidal remains the best place for artists to share their work, and for listeners to enjoy it, we’re removing all tracks that we determine are 100% AI generated," Tidal said in a social media post on Tuesday. "We’re also banning distributors from delivering these tracks to us, and will reject deliveries if their metadata says they were generated solely using AI tools."

Tracks that were made with assistance from AI will still be allowed. The new ban will go into effect December 9.

Tidal said it's seen an influx of AI-generated tracks on its platform over the past several months, noting that in the past 90 days, about 43 percent of tracks distributed on the platform were identified as wholly AI-generated. On Nov. 6 alone, 60 percent of newly uploaded songs were AI tracks. But despite the growing number of songs, 96 percent of those tracks have generated zero streams.

"Wholly AI-generated music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists is another serious problem that has only increased in scale," Tidal said. "It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried."

With its decision Tuesday, Tidal now has the most stringent anti-AI policies among the music streaming services, and one of the few notable platforms beyond Bandcamp, the music distribution service popular among indie artists, to have outright banned AI music. While Spotify and Apple Music, the two largest DSPs, have taken steps to either label AI tracks and artists or remove them from recommendations, they still allow fully-generated songs to get uploaded to their respective platforms.

Fans and the music industry alike have voiced their frustration about AI music flooding streaming platforms. On an earnings call in October , Universal Music Group CEO Lucian Grainge advocated for streaming services to pay out AI-generated tracks less than music from human artists, arguing that AI slop degrades the fan experience and diverts value from real artists," and that removing the profit motive would disincentivize “industrial scale content production.”

I had the privilege of interviewing the cast ahead of the movie's release, where I asked Hawke if any scenes of her character ended up on the cutting room floor. She told me:

Despite being a franchise about young people killing each other, The Hunger Games movies have all been PG-13. As such, Lawrence and company have to be specific about how violent the imagery can be. While I wanted to see more of Wiress, Hawke maintains that it would have been too "disturbing" to watch the beloved Victor being tortured by President Snow's forces. She's probably not wrong, as much as I wanted to see more of her take on the character.

Later in our same conversation, Maya Hawke explained the upside of not having to shoot these difficult scenes as Wiress. As she told me:

Obviously Hawke would have crushed it if we saw Wiress' torture and interrogation, but that ultimately wasn't something that was ever going to be part of Sunrise on the Reaping. The movie had to cut plenty of scenes like Maysilee killing a Gamemaker , although that wasn't the case for Hawke's character.

In our chat I asked the Do Revenge actress if Wiress had a mental break as a result of her torture, transforming her into the character we were introduced to by Amanda Plummer in Catching Fire . She confirmed to me:

I've still got FOMO about not getting more of Wiress, but I understand why it didn't happen. After all, Sunrise on the Reaping is a story about Haymitch above all. There was a ton of content to stuff into the movie's 158-minute runtime, so there was only so much time to dedicate to characters like Wiress and Mags.
